recaps.headline: So much for inevitable
body: Last week this column closed with the commissioner quoting Thanos at a man he had just beaten by 57.54. Seven days later Coyne4 posted the highest score in the division, ended the only unbeaten run in either league, and watched Ehoeff3 lose to a 2-4 team. Nothing, it turns out, was inevitable.
## Premier League — Week 7

Coyne4 158.38, TySpaltholz 114.24. Six and oh is over, and the man who ended it is the one this column spent five weeks inventing a losing record for. Joe Burrow went 28.88, nine of his ten starters cleared eight points, and Ty — who put 226.96 on the board a fortnight ago — managed 114.24, his lowest of the season. Drake Maye's 28.44 was most of it.
The Premier League podium goes to Coyne4, who answered in the only dialect this league speaks:

body.quote: The Standard is the Standard. — Mike Tomlin
body.note: 158.38 — Premier League high, Week 7, and the end of TySpaltholz's unbeaten run

body: Two things about that. The first is that Hayden Hairston said the same sentence at this podium in Week 4, from the other division, without the attribution. Three weeks later it comes back with the credit attached and a scalp underneath it. The second is that Coyne4 has started the Pittsburgh defence in consecutive weeks, so the Tomlin citation is not a bit.
He also won it with Tre Tucker's 21.30 on the bench, the second week running he has left that particular player out and the first week it has not mattered.

KyleRobertson45 133.22, Ehoeff3 124.32. Last week this column noted that KyleRobertson45 had opened with 172.86 and gone backwards ever since, and that he had started DJ Moore for nothing while leaving Trevor Lawrence on the bench. On Sunday he put up his best score since Week 1 and beat the commissioner by 8.90. The commissioner is 4-3.
The ledger continues not to flatter this desk: Coyne4's career record is 29-23. Ehoeff3's is 27-25. That gap was two games a week ago. It is now four.

bencawyer 152.90, TheGloveDidntFit 106.02. Tony Pollard 36.50, the largest single-player score in the division this week. That is three straight wins for a man who was 0-4 on October 6 and being measured for relegation in this space. He is 3-4, fifth, and back inside the playoff six on the fourth-most points.
Glove's 106.02 is the division's lowest score of the week and his own worst of the season. He is sixth, holding the last playoff place by five points.

quinnmurray 139.26, kcjaeb 125.02. Four straight. quinnmurray was 0-3 and the subject of an obituary in this column; he is 4-3 and fourth, and he has done it on the eighth-most points in a ten-team division. Since the trade with Glove on October 2 he has gone 4-0. kcjaeb drops out of the six.

jackfierro 135.40, PeterNell 123.22. jackfierro did it while starting a defence that scored minus four, which tells you what the other nine were doing. PeterNell is 2-5, last, and alone at the bottom on the fewest points in the division.
## The Premier League table

TySpaltholz 6-1 and still clear. Then three teams at 4-3 — Ehoeff3, Coyne4, quinnmurray — and then five teams at 3-4: bencawyer, TheGloveDidntFit, kcjaeb, jackfierro, KyleRobertson45. PeterNell is 2-5.

The playoff line falls between sixth and seventh, and it is currently five points wide. TheGloveDidntFit 943.80, kcjaeb 938.80. jackfierro is a further 2.38 back. Sixth, seventh and eighth are separated by 7.38 points across seven weeks of football.

One correction to last week, which did not survive the weekend. This column reported that TySpaltholz now held the best career record in league history outright, having passed bencawyer. Ty lost, bencawyer won, and they are level again at 33-21. The claim lasted six days. There is a pattern here and it is not flattering.
## G.R.I.T. League — Week 7

hhairston 185.74, Tvas22 168.60. Jameson Williams 26.10, four more starters past 19, and a response to his first back-to-back defeats of the season. hhairston is 5-2 and level with danielbelardi1 at the top.
The G.R.I.T. League podium goes to hhairston, who stayed on theme:

body.quote: It ain't about how hard you hit. It's about how hard you can get hit and keep moving forward

body: Rocky, and reasonable. He had lost two in a row for the first time since he joined this league, including a Week 6 defeat to shaw5. He got hit and he moved forward. It is also the second week running that a podium quote has arrived pre-loaded with a sporting cliche delivered entirely straight, which this column has decided to enjoy rather than resist.

colehanna22 177.70, CaptWong 172.60. He won. After six weeks of this column cataloguing the gap between what colehanna22 scores and what he gets for it, he put up 177.70 and took it by 5.10. It is his second win of the season.

It has moved him from eighth to seventh. He is 2-5 with the third-most points in the division, which is exactly where he was a week ago, and the 1,203.46 he has scored is more than everybody below first and second. At some point this stops being a talking point and starts being a season.
danielbelardi1 152.02, shaw5 76.04. chrismarzo 149.52, BalineseBandit 71.22. Both winners scored under 153. Both won by more than 75.
## The two worst scores in this division's history, in the same week

BalineseBandit 71.22. shaw5 76.04. Those are the lowest and second-lowest totals ever recorded in the superflex division, and they were posted on the same Sunday, in a format that inflates scoring so much that this column has to caveat every record it sets.

BalineseBandit started six players who scored 0.00 out of a twelve-man lineup, and left Joe Burrow and his 28.88 on the bench — the same 28.88 that won Coyne4 the Premier League podium an hour up the road. shaw5 started four players on zero, a defence that went minus two, and left 84.42 points unused.
BalineseBandit now owns three of the six lowest scores in the division's history. Two of them have come in the last fortnight: 98.76 in Week 6, 71.22 in Week 7.

This column is not going to guess at why, and byes and injuries are real. But six zeros in a starting twelve is not a bad week, it is an unset lineup, and two of them landing in the same round of fixtures is a competitive problem rather than a joke — chrismarzo and danielbelardi1 both collected comfortable wins they did not have to earn, in a division where three of eight teams go up. That is the commissioner's to look at, not this column's.
## The G.R.I.T. League table

danielbelardi1 5-2 and hhairston 5-2 at the top. Tvas22 4-3 and CaptWong 4-3 completing the four. Then chrismarzo 3-4 on the fifth-most points, shaw5 3-4 on the seventh, colehanna22 2-5 on the third, BalineseBandit 2-5 on the eighth.

chrismarzo is fifth and out by one game, having said at this podium last week that he intended to run the table. He won, which keeps it technically alive; he now needs the other seven. Seven weeks remain in the G.R.I.T. regular season and only three of the four qualifiers are promoted.
## Rivalry watch

Nothing. No configured rivalry was on the schedule in either division. PeterNell vs TheGloveDidntFit remains the only playable one that has not been staged in 2026; they last met in Week 12 of 2025 and both are now in trouble, which should make it worth the wait.
## Week 8

The Premier League has turned into a two-tier problem. TySpaltholz is 6-1 and the three teams at 4-3 are all plausible; the five teams at 3-4 are separated by 125 points of scoring and nothing else, and four of them will be in the drop bracket when the music stops. The five-point gap between sixth and seventh is the whole story from here.

In G.R.I.T., the top four have separated and the question is which of them finishes fourth, because fourth and out is the same as eighth and out. colehanna22 has the third-most points, two wins, and seven games to make the arithmetic mean something. And the division's two worst totals ever were set on the same afternoon, which is the part worth watching for reasons that have nothing to do with football.

recaps.headline: The correction lasted six days
body: Last Monday this column printed a correction. It had claimed, three separate times, that Coyne4 had never beaten the commissioner — an 0-6 record that was never in the Sleeper data and came instead from this desk. The true figure was 3-3. The correction ran on the 13th. On the 18th the commissioner dropped 156.96 on Coyne4, won by 57.54, and made it 4-3. The apology stands. The timing is a disgrace.
## Premier League — Week 6

Ehoeff3 156.96, Coyne4 99.42. The one rivalry on the configured list that had gone the entire season unplayed — flagged here in Week 4 as still sitting in the schedule, flagged again in Week 5 — came off the board in the most lopsided way available. Tyler Shough went 26.96 at quarterback. Coyne4 posted his only sub-100 of the year, 34.89 below his own weekly average, and did it with Tre Tucker's 26.70 on the bench. It was over by the late window.
The Premier League podium goes to Ehoeff3, who had evidently been working on something all week:

body.quote: Coyne could not live with his own failure... and where did that bring you? back to me. I am... Inevitable.

body: That is a Thanos line, delivered by a man who had just been publicly handed back three wins he spent a season pretending his opponent never got. There was a version of this week where the commissioner took the result quietly. This was not it.

And since the ledger ought to be right for once: the series is 4-3 counting every meeting, 3-2 on regular-season games alone, and 1-1 in the playoffs. Coyne4's career record is 28-23. The commissioner's is 27-24. Across four seasons Coyne4 has won a higher share of his games than the man who writes about him, and the only reason anybody reading this believed otherwise is that this column told them so.

TySpaltholz 149.90, PeterNell 103.18. Six and oh. The most points in the division, the fewest problems, and a win this week that required nothing much — PeterNell has not reached 140 in a single week this season and his 699.90 is the lowest total in the Premier League. Ty's career record is now 33-20, the best in this league outright. bencawyer had been level with him on Monday. He is not any more.

quinnmurray 123.34, KyleRobertson45 86.20. Three straight. A man who was 0-3 and being eulogised in this space is 3-3 and sixth, which is the last playoff place, on the eighth-most points in the division. That is not a good team yet. It is a team that has stopped losing, which on a ten-team ladder with four drop slots is most of the job.

KyleRobertson45 opened the season with 172.86 and has not been close since: 132.62, 104.78, 75.78, 131.04, 86.20. On Sunday he started DJ Moore for zero and left Trevor Lawrence's 28.34 on the bench. He is 2-4 and ninth, and the first week of September is doing an enormous amount of work in his points total.

TheGloveDidntFit 137.28, kcjaeb 113.40. The Glove up to third, his high-water mark for the season, and kcjaeb's three-week run is over. Both are 3-3, both are inside the six, and neither has done a single thing to suggest that is permanent.

bencawyer 123.10, jackfierro 111.52. Two in a row for the man who needed five weeks to get one, and it has moved him precisely nowhere. bencawyer is 2-4 and seventh — in the relegation bracket — on the fifth-most points in the division. He is the sharpest case in either league of the table and the scoreboard disagreeing, and the table is the one that relegates you.
## The Premier League table

TySpaltholz 6-0 and clear. Ehoeff3 4-2. Then four teams at 3-3 filling out the playoff six — TheGloveDidntFit, kcjaeb, Coyne4, quinnmurray. Then four teams at 2-4, all of them in the drop bracket: bencawyer, jackfierro, KyleRobertson45, PeterNell.
The team in seventh has scored 14.14 more points than the team in sixth. Seven weeks left. Nobody below Ehoeff3 is safe and nobody above jackfierro is finished.
## G.R.I.T. League — Week 6

chrismarzo 177.72, colehanna22 159.82. Christian McCaffrey 30.70, Trevor Lawrence 28.34, and the division's best score of the week. chrismarzo has now gone between 158.76 and 184.88 in all six weeks of this season — a 26.12-point spread, the tightest of anybody in either league — and he is 2-4.
The G.R.I.T. League podium goes to chrismarzo, who has done the arithmetic:

body.quote: I feel like we can run the table - Aaron Rodgers

body: Eight games remain in a fourteen-week regular season. Running the table from 2-4 means winning all eight and finishing 10-4, which would almost certainly promote him. Rodgers said it in 2016 at 4-6 and then won six straight, so the precedent is real — it is also the most quoted piece of optimism in modern sport precisely because the people repeating it usually do not get there.

In his favour: he is sixth on the fifth-most points, the top five in scoring are separated by 129.64 points, and he has not had a bad week all year. Against him: six games, two wins. It is not the stupidest thing anybody has said in this league.
## About colehanna22
He is 1-5. He has the third-most points in the division. Both are true and only one of them is interesting.

The full ledger: 150.06, 179.60, 172.74, 170.56, 192.98, 159.82. He has not had a bad week. He has not had a great one either — his best is 192.98, and that number has been beaten somewhere in these two leagues eight times this season. What he has is six solid weeks and one win, and the one win came against the lowest total anybody has put on him all year.

The comparison that actually matters is shaw5, who has scored 896.86 points — the fewest in the division, 128.90 fewer than colehanna22. shaw5 is 3-3 and fifth. colehanna22 is 1-5 and eighth. Two more wins on 128.90 fewer points.

And the other one: colehanna22 1025.76, Tvas22 1025.56, chrismarzo 1023.78. Three teams inside 1.98 points of each other across six weeks, with records of 1-5, 4-2 and 2-4. The scoring table is not telling anybody anything they can spend.

So yes, he has been unlucky, and the schedule has been genuinely vicious — five of his six opponents cleared 176. But on Sunday he lost by 17.90 with Bryce Young's 19.84 and Luther Burden's 17.50 sitting on his bench: 37.34 points he had already paid for and declined to use. Last week he was fourth in scoring. This week he is third in scoring and last in the table. Climbing one list while sliding down the other is not a schedule problem.

CaptWong 152.04, danielbelardi1 122.20. The leader's worst week of the season by 29.50 and his first defeat since Week 2. daniel is still first on 1153.42, still 70.48 clear of anyone, still 4-2 — the damage is cosmetic. CaptWong is 4-2 and fourth and has now won three of four since putting up 118.82 in Week 2.

shaw5 159.00, hhairston 133.28. Back-to-back defeats for hhairston after four straight wins, and 133.28 is his worst week of the year by 41.92. Winning is a burden, but someone has to carry it was his Week 4 line; the burden got set down for a fortnight. He is still 4-2 and second on points. shaw5 is 3-3 and fifth on the fewest points in the division — either the most efficient season anybody is having or a bill that arrives in November.

Tvas22 148.48, BalineseBandit 98.76. Balinese scored 210.60 in Week 5 and 98.76 in Week 6, a collapse of 111.84 in seven days, and he managed it by starting four players who scored nothing at all while leaving 65.62 points on the bench. It is the lowest score anybody has posted in this division this season. Tvas22 is 4-2 and third.
## The G.R.I.T. League table

Four teams at 4-2, and they are exactly the four playoff places: danielbelardi1, hhairston, Tvas22, CaptWong, in that order on points. shaw5 3-3 and fifth. chrismarzo and BalineseBandit 2-4. colehanna22 1-5.

Eight weeks left — and remember that only three of the four playoff teams go up: the champion, the runner-up and the winner of the third-place game. Making the bracket and losing twice is worth nothing at all.
## Rivalry watch
The last one fired. Ehoeff3 vs Coyne4 was the only configured rivalry in either league that had not been played in 2026, and the commissioner took it 156.96–99.42 to lead the series 4-3.

One fix to last week's note, which listed four unplayed rivalries. KyleRobertson45 vs kcjaeb was not one of them — they met in Week 1 and Kyle won 172.86–136.06. The genuine remainder is PeterNell vs TheGloveDidntFit, who have not shared a schedule slot since Week 12 of 2025. BalineseBandit vs jackfierro can no longer happen; they are in different divisions now.
## Week 7

TySpaltholz is 6-0 on the most points in the division and there is no longer an argument to make against him. The interesting half of the Premier League is the bottom, where four teams sit at 2-4 and the relegation bracket is currently occupied by the fifth-, seventh-, ninth- and tenth-highest scorers in the division. Three of those four go down unless they win the consolation bracket — and bencawyer is in there holding the second-best career record of anyone who has played more than one season.

In G.R.I.T., four teams at 4-2 and the whole division covered by three wins. colehanna22 needs the schedule to relent and is not owed it. chrismarzo has eight games to run the table and has announced as much, which means the rest of the division now gets to watch him try.

recaps.headline: The schedule merchant would like a word
body: For three weeks this column filed the same complaint about TySpaltholz. Unbeaten, yes — but on the eighth-most points, then the fifth-most, a man collecting wins out of other people's bad Sundays. On Sunday he scored 226.96, beat the commissioner by 115.02, and took over first place in scoring on his way past. The complaint is withdrawn in full and with some embarrassment.
## Premier League — Week 5

TySpaltholz 226.96, Ehoeff3 111.94. Understand what that number is. The highest score ever recorded in this league outside the superflex division is no longer 183.46 — PeterNell, 2023, Week 4. It is this. Ty beat a four-year-old league record by 43.50 points, in the week the column had spent a fortnight insisting he was a fraud, against the man who publishes the column. He is 5-0, first in the table and first in points. There is no longer an argument to have.
The Premier League podium goes to TySpaltholz, and he arrived at it with a prepared statement:

body.quote: Wow. No longer just a schedule merchant. We're here.

body: We're here. He is. The schedule-merchant charge was this column's, it was filed in Week 3 and renewed in Week 4, and it has now been answered by the largest score in the history of the standard-scoring game. Ty did not just beat the allegation; he beat it by 43 points over a record set by a man currently ninth. The commissioner, for his part, posted his worst number of the season while it was happening. Everyone involved got exactly what they deserved.

bencawyer 151.20, PeterNell 139.90. He won. After four defeats, two of them by a combined 0.90 points, the joint-holder of the best career record in league history finally converted. He is 1-4 and still bottom, and here is the cruel symmetry of his season: for three weeks he led the division in scoring and lost anyway; now that he has started winning, he has slipped to seventh in points. He has had the production and the result at no point simultaneously.

quinnmurray 157.94, Coyne4 141.88. Two in a row. The man who scored 81.04 in Week 3 and was written off in this column has won back-to-back games, is 2-3, and has climbed to seventh. Last week he announced the return of Team name TBD nation on the back of one good afternoon; it has since become a run. Coyne4 drops to 3-2 and third, which is still a fine season for a man who is 3-3 against the commissioner across six career meetings, including a 1-1 split in the playoffs.

kcjaeb 145.04, jackfierro 114.42. Three straight. kcjaeb is 3-2 and fourth, inside the playoff places, having been picked in the season preview to go straight back down on the strength of a 14-25 career record. He has now beaten bencawyer, PeterNell and jackfierro in consecutive weeks. The preview is looking worse every Monday. jackfierro is 2-3 and sixth — the last safe seat, for the third week running, with the division's sixth-most points and a quote from Week 1 still outstanding.

TheGloveDidntFit 135.52, KyleRobertson45 131.04. By 4.48, and it moved Glove out of the drop zone and back into the safe six at fifth. KyleRobertson45 is 2-3 and eighth, with the ninth-most points in a ten-team league. He was top of the table after Week 2. Since then: 104.78, 75.78, 131.04. Whatever that start was, it has left the building and taken the furniture.

The drop zone reads quinnmurray, KyleRobertson45, PeterNell, bencawyer — and the three teams in seventh, eighth and ninth are all 2-3, separated by points alone. Nothing down there is settled by anything except next Sunday.
## G.R.I.T. League — Week 5

danielbelardi1 222.48, hhairston 218.44. First against second, 4.04 points between them, and the lead in the division changed hands. danielbelardi1 is 4-1 and the only team in either league past 1,000 points — 1,031.22, eighty-two clear of the field. hhairston's unbeaten run ends at four in the best game of the season anywhere.

The G.R.I.T. League podium goes to danielbelardi1 for the third time in five weeks. In Week 3 he explained that he had stopped going to Sunday mass because this team brought him more joy than God. The theological position has since hardened:

body.quote: I am not in danger, Skylar. I am the danger. I am the one who knocks.

body: So the arc of this man's season runs: skips church, becomes Heisenberg, takes first place. Three podiums, the two biggest scores in the division's history, a four-point win over the only other team with a claim to the title, and a leaguewide points lead. He is not in danger. On the available evidence he is, in fact, the danger. The remaining seven managers are invited to knock back.

BalineseBandit 210.60, shaw5 119.08. A 91.52-point beating, the widest margin anywhere this week, from the man whose Week 2 podium address promised he would never surrender and whose Week 4 performance surrendered by 87. He is 2-3 and fifth. shaw5 posted the lowest score in either division and sits sixth.

colehanna22 192.98, Tvas22 165.58. The first win of colehanna22's season, and he will want it noted that he has the fourth-most points in the division. He does. In a league of eight. Three teams score more than him and four score fewer, which is the dictionary definition of the middle — and his 192.98 was, fittingly, the fourth-best score of the week. He has been the fourth-best thing in every room he has entered this season, and he is 1-4 and seventh, because the teams above him keep converting points into wins, which remains the mechanism by which the game is played. The luck has been genuinely bad. The team is genuinely fine. Both of those can be true and neither of them is a trophy.

CaptWong 188.46, chrismarzo 158.76. CaptWong is 3-2 and fourth, inside the promotion places, with the seventh-most points in an eight-team division. That is now a five-week-old arrangement and it has stopped looking like a fluke and started looking like a strategy nobody can explain. chrismarzo is 1-4 and bottom with the fifth-most points — the mirror image, and no happier for it.

The promotion places read danielbelardi1, hhairston, Tvas22, CaptWong. The two teams with the best records are also the two best-scoring teams, which is the first time this division has made sense all year. Below them it reverts immediately to nonsense: fifth through eighth contains the fourth- and fifth-most productive teams in the league.
## Rivalry watch

Nothing. For the first time this season not one of the ten configured rivalries was on the schedule in either division. Four remain unplayed: PeterNell vs TheGloveDidntFit, KyleRobertson45 vs kcjaeb, BalineseBandit vs jackfierro and Ehoeff3 vs Coyne4 — the last of those dead level at 3-3 after six meetings, which gets more conspicuous the longer the fixture list declines to schedule it.
## Week 6

The Premier League has one unbeaten team and it is no longer a punchline. TySpaltholz is 5-0 with the most points in the division, which removes the only argument anyone had against him and leaves the rest of the league with the more difficult problem of actually beating him.

Five teams are 2-3. Three of them are in the relegation bracket and two are not, and the entire difference is points scored. If you are sitting seventh, eighth or ninth, the fastest route out is not a win — it is a big win.

And bencawyer has one. It took five weeks, a share of the best career record in this league's history, and 685 points to get there. Whether it is the start of something or the only one he gets is the most interesting question left in the division.
## Correction

This column got things wrong and they are worth setting straight. Coyne4 has beaten the commissioner. The 0-6 record printed here three times was never in the data — it came from this desk. The true record is 3-3 across six meetings, or 2-2 if you count only the regular season: Ehoeff3 in 2023 Week 6, 2024 Week 1 and the 2024 postseason; Coyne4 in the 2023 postseason, 2024 Week 12 and 2025 Week 5.

Three smaller ones. quinnmurray has never defended a title — he won in 2023 and 2025, with TySpaltholz's 2024 sitting in between, so "two-time defending champion" was wrong both times it appeared. The TySpaltholz–bencawyer series had three postseason meetings in seven, not "mostly". And bencawyer no longer owns the best career record outright: Ty's 5-0 start has pulled him level at 28-16 apiece.

One structural note, because it explains why the Rivalries tab and this column have disagreed. The tab counts every game ever played, including the postseason and the consolation bracket. This column has been quoting regular-season records. Both are honest; neither was labelled. On the tab's basis TySpaltholz already has the best record in league history at 32-20. Everything else checked out, including the 128.80-point beatdown, the 185.62 all-time high, and every other rivalry record on the site.

recaps.headline: A Friday night trade, and the 81-point man buries the commissioner
body: Last Monday this column printed the commissioner's own description of his office as a burden, and noted that nine men were in a position to lighten the load. It took six days. It was not one of the nine. It was the tenth — bottom of the table, 0-3, coming off the worst score anybody had managed all season, and forty-two hours removed from the biggest trade of the year.
## The trade
Friday night, 10:31pm. TheGloveDidntFit and quinnmurray. Three players each.

Glove sent out Ashton Jeanty, Quinshon Judkins and Tetairoa McMillan and received Nico Collins, DeVonta Smith and Travis Etienne. Youth and upside in one direction, proven production in the other. Two teams sitting seventh and tenth, both inside the consolation bracket, both arriving at the same conclusion on the same evening: the roster I have is not the roster I want.

Forty-two hours later quinnmurray posted 168.40 — the highest score in the Premier League — and won his first game of the season. Glove posted 148.62, his second-best number of the year, and lost by four-tenths of a point.
Nobody should draw a conclusion from one weekend. Everybody is going to. The ledger on this one gets settled in December, and this site is keeping both columns of it from here.

The margin of 109.76 is the second-biggest in league history. There is an asterisk, because the G.R.I.T. League is superflex and scores run hot down here. He will never acknowledge the asterisk and honestly he has earned that.

shaw5 175.76, Tvas22 170.14. The newest rivalry in the league opened with a 5.62-point decision, which is about as good a first chapter as anyone could ask for. It also decides more than it looks: only four of eight make the playoffs down here, and that 5.62 is currently the difference between shaw5 in fourth and Tvas22 in fifth, which is the difference between a promotion shot and a wasted year.

CaptWong 187.46, BalineseBandit 129.38. CaptWong announces himself with the second-highest score in the division. BalineseBandit — the only man in this league who was above .500 last season, and the preview's pick to go straight back up — posted the lowest score of the week and sits dead last. hhairston 176.70, chrismarzo 160.96 settled the debutants' derby, and hhairston is third with a real score in his first ever fantasy week in this league.
The G.R.I.T. table now splits exactly along the playoff line: the four winners are in, the four losers are out, and Tvas22 missed the cut by 5.62 points. Fourteen weeks to fix it.
## Rivalry watch

Three new rivalries were added this week and two of them played immediately. Coyne4 finally beat bencawyer after four straight losses. shaw5 edged Tvas22 by under six in the first meeting they have ever had. The third — Ehoeff3 vs jackfierro — did not play, which is a shame, because the archive on that one is live: the commissioner leads 3-2 all-time but jackfierro has won the last two, including a 2025 playoff game that ended Ehoeff3's season 112.60 to 102.20. That one is going to be worth a flag when it comes around.
## Week 2

The Premier League drop zone is going to look very different by Sunday night, because it always does in September. What will not change is the shape of the thing: jackfierro, KyleRobertson45 and Coyne4 all opened with top-three scores and look like they meant it, while quinnmurray, TheGloveDidntFit and PeterNell have work to do and one fewer week to do it in. Note that the Premier League's regular season runs thirteen weeks, not fourteen — playoffs start in Week 14 up top and Week 15 down in the G.R.I.T. League. The top flight has less time to sort itself out than the division below it.
Everything on this site updates itself. Check the odds page before you talk trash — it now has an actual week of data to work with, and it is not impressed by most of you.

recaps.headline: Eighteen teams, one ladder, and nowhere to hide
body: Eighteen managers. Two leagues. One ladder connecting them, with a trapdoor at the bottom of the good one. After three seasons of everybody crammed into the same room pretending 12th place meant nothing, the PAC2PAC finally has consequences.

The rules, because they will decide somebody's December. Premier League: top six make the playoffs and are safe. The other four fall into a consolation bracket where only the winner stays up — the other three are relegated to the G.R.I.T. League for 2027. G.R.I.T. League: only the top four make the playoffs, and three of those four go up — champion, runner-up, and the winner of the third-place game. Finish fifth down there and your season is over in every sense that matters. There is $900 in the pot and every dollar goes out. The money is the small print. The group chat will be about who gets to stay.

A term you will see on this site constantly: six-pointer. Borrowed from English football, where a win is worth three points, so beating a team level with you is worth six — three you gain, three they don't. Fantasy has no points for a win, but the logic survives the trip: when two clubs outside the top six play each other, the winner climbs and the loser sinks, and the gap between them moves by two games instead of one. Those are the games that decide who goes down — not the blowouts against good teams, but the grubby Week 11 fixture between two 4-6 sides who both know exactly what is at stake.
## The champions

Three seasons, three titles, two names. quinnmurray owns two of them — 2023 and 2025 — and TySpaltholz took 2024 by beating TheGloveDidntFit in the final. That is the entire history of this league's silverware, and everyone else is playing catch-up.

quinnmurray's reign deserves proper examination, because it makes no sense. His career regular-season record is 20-19. He went 5-8 in 2024. He has never finished first in the regular season, never had the most points, and has never been anyone's preseason favourite. He has also won the whole thing twice, most recently by beating an 11-2 bencawyer in the final while sitting on a 7-6 record himself. He is not the best manager in this league. He is simply the one holding the trophy, twice, and that has always been the only statistic that counts.
## Beatdowns of the past

The record book is not kind reading. The most violent thing that has ever happened in this league came in Week 12 of 2025, when TheGloveDidntFit beat PeterNell 178.42 to 49.62 — a margin of 128.80 points, and by some distance the worst afternoon anyone has had here. PeterNell's 49.62 is also the lowest score in recorded league history. One game, two records, same victim.

PeterNell's archive is a genuinely remarkable document. He owns the lowest score ever (49.62), the third-lowest (54.10), and the second-highest (183.46, Week 4 of 2023). Nobody in this league has ever been simultaneously this good and this bad. The all-time high belongs to KyleRobertson45 — 185.62, in a 2024 playoff game, which remains the single best performance anyone has produced when it mattered.

Honourable mentions in the beatdown ledger: colehanna22 165.90–62.36 over shaw5 in 2024, Coyne4 149.82–54.10 over PeterNell in 2023, and quinnmurray 182.98–97.86 over shaw5 in 2023. shaw5 appears in this paragraph twice and also owns two of the five lowest scores ever recorded. He is in the G.R.I.T. League now, and the file explains why.
## The rivalries
Seven of them, and the archive has receipts on every pair that has actually met.

TySpaltholz vs bencawyer is the real one. Seven meetings, bencawyer leads 4-3, and they have played each other in the playoffs three years running — 2023, 2024 and 2025. No other pair in this league is close to that. Last January bencawyer ended Ty's season 149.34 to 95.22.

PeterNell vs TheGloveDidntFit is 2-1 to Glove and contains the 128-point demolition described above, which means this rivalry is less a rivalry than a documented crime. Ehoeff3 vs Coyne4 sits dead level at 3-3 across six meetings including two playoff games, which is the most annoying possible score for both men. KyleRobertson45 vs kcjaeb — this week's fixture — is 2-2, meaning kcjaeb, owner of a 14-25 career record, is somehow break-even against a man who has been to a final. It is his one demonstrable talent.

BalineseBandit vs jackfierro have met exactly once: jackfierro won 164.90 to 110.76 in Week 2 of 2025. That result now stands frozen forever, because they are in different leagues. No fixture, no rematch, no way to settle it. One of them has to climb or the other has to fall. It is either the cruellest thing about this format or the best argument for it. hhairston vs CaptWong and chrismarzo vs Tvas22 start from nothing — all four are new, with no history to lean on and nothing to avenge yet.
## Premier League — Week 1

TySpaltholz vs TheGloveDidntFit. The 2024 championship game, replayed in Week 1, because Sleeper's schedule generator has a crueller sense of humour than anyone in this league. Glove went 10-3 that year — the best record in the league — and lost the only game that mattered. He responded by going 5-8 the following season. Three years in he is 19-20 lifetime with one final appearance and nothing in the case. Ty has the ring. Ty will mention the ring.

bencawyer vs Coyne4. Fifty combined regular-season wins. Zero combined championships. bencawyer owns the best career record in league history at 27-12, including an 11-2 season that ended with him losing the final to a 7-6 team. Coyne4 has the highest career scoring average of anyone in the league at 132.7 a week, has never had a losing season, and has also never won anything. Two men who are extremely good at the part of the year that doesn't count.

jackfierro vs quinnmurray. The reigning champion opens against a man who is 17-22 lifetime and has never finished above the middle. On paper this is straightforward. On paper quinnmurray was 5-8 the year before he won it, so paper has a poor record here.

kcjaeb vs KyleRobertson45. The only rivalry drawn in Week 1. Kyle is 23-16 with a runner-up finish, a third-place game and the highest score ever recorded. kcjaeb is 14-25 with seasons of 4-9, 4-9 and 6-7 — a man who has never once been good, in any year, at any point. The head-to-head is 2-2. Football is not fair.

Ehoeff3 vs PeterNell. Your commissioner has gone 8-5, 7-6 and 7-6, has never reached a final, and has just written a set of rules that relegates three people for being mediocre. PeterNell arrives holding the worst single performance in league history. One of these men starts 1-0 and neither should feel good about it.
## G.R.I.T. League — Week 1

And the maths down here just got vicious. Only four of the eight make the playoffs, and three of those four are promoted. There is no cushion, no soft landing, no consolation prize for a good regular season — finish fifth and you are stuck in the G.R.I.T. League for another year regardless of how well you played. Effectively, the regular season is the promotion race, and the bracket is just the formality that decides which three of the four survivors get the ticket. Every week from here is a playoff.

First, the thing that has to be said. kcjaeb and shaw5 have the exact same career record: 14-25. Same wins, same losses, three seasons each of being equally, identically bad. Then 2025 happened — kcjaeb went 6-7, shaw5 went 5-8 — and one game separated them forever. kcjaeb is in the Premier League. shaw5 is down here, opening against Tvas22, a man with no league history whatsoever. Three years of parity undone by a single result.

danielbelardi1 vs colehanna22 pits last season's worst team — 3-10, no ambiguity — against the highest-scoring manager in this league's history at 124.9 a week, a man who has nonetheless gone 7-6, 6-7 and 6-7 and appears to have taken a blood oath never to finish more than one game from .500. CaptWong vs BalineseBandit is the closest thing to a marquee fixture down here, and chrismarzo vs hhairston puts the two managers with no record at all directly against each other, guaranteeing exactly one of them starts their PAC2PAC career 0-1.

One structural warning for whoever climbs out: the G.R.I.T. League is superflex. Twelve starters, a second quarterback, scores a mile higher than the Premier League's. Get promoted and you will spend an entire draft discovering that everything you learned down here was calibrated for a different sport.
## What we think happens

If three years of scoring means anything — and it usually does — the Premier League's drop bracket is already taking shape. The four lowest career scoring averages in the top flight belong to TheGloveDidntFit (124.0), jackfierro (121.6), PeterNell (121.4) and kcjaeb (115.7). Those are your four favourites for the consolation bracket, and three of them will go down. kcjaeb in particular is nine points a week behind the league's best scorer, which across fourteen games is not variance, it is a gap.

At the top, Coyne4 and bencawyer have the best claim on paper — the highest scoring average and the best record in league history respectively — and both have precisely nothing to show for their careers, which is exactly the kind of streak that ends in a title or another year of complaining. quinnmurray should not be favoured and will probably win it anyway.

In the G.R.I.T. League, colehanna22 arrives as the best scorer with a real record and BalineseBandit as the only man down here who was above .500 last season. But half that league is brand new, the format is superflex, and only four of eight make the bracket — which is the great equaliser. Nobody's history tells you much about how they draft two quarterbacks, and with three of four playoff teams going up, one hot October from a total unknown is the whole ballgame. Genuinely wide open, and the only one of the two leagues where somebody with no record at all could be in the Premier League by January.
## Good luck

Games kick off Thursday. Scores update every minute on Sundays, the tables and the drop zone update themselves, the odds re-run in your browser every time you open them, and there will be a written recap every Tuesday naming whoever most deserves it.

To the eighteen of you: this is the first year any of this has meant anything beyond a group chat. Somebody is going to win $500. Somebody is going to spend December fighting for their life in a consolation bracket. Three of you in the Premier League will not be here next year, and three of you in the G.R.I.T. League are going to take their places. Good luck to all of you, sincerely. Most of you will need it.
